title: Embroidered the spectral cutlass — finished piece

posts.cooked:
Hey everyone, just wanted to share a little project I finally wrapped up—an embroidered version of the Spectral Cutlass from our favorite ghostly seas adventure! I’ve been sitting on this idea since the remastered wave hit because the intricate glow and ethereal details really called for a mix of stitching techniques. I used a combination of subtle silver threads and some glow-in-the-dark filament to try and capture that haunting shimmer you see in the game. It was tricky to balance, but I’m super happy with how it catches the light in different angles.

Since the original in-game model gets updated with the modded remaster, I incorporated some of those rare patterns from the expanded lore, so it feels like a tangible piece of that deeper story. It’s been fun seeing how a digital weapon can inspire something tactile and, honestly, makes me appreciate the design even more now that I’ve put so much time into recreating it by hand.

Would love to hear what you think or if anyone else is working on fan-made stuff inspired by the remaster! I’m thinking of doing a matching sheath or maybe a cosplay accessory next. Also, if anyone’s interested, I can share some of my stitching notes or the pattern template I made. Thanks for checking it out!

posts.cooked:
Wow, this looks absolutely stunning! I love how you managed to capture the eerie glow of the spectral blade with the embroidery — it really feels like the cutlass could slice right through the fabric. The detailed threads for the ghostly flames are such a nice touch, it reminds me of the way it flickers in the remastered cutscene. I’m guessing you used that new thread variant from the latest dye pack? It definitely gives it that otherworldly shimmer.

Also, huge props on the handle design. The way the hilt twists and merges with the ethereal mist is something I’ve never seen done in textile form before. It’s crazy to think about how you translated a modded weapon from the game’s files into something you can actually hold and admire outside the screen. Have you thought about making a small series based on other iconic weapons from the haunted seas update? I’d definitely be first in line to see what you come up with next!

posts.cooked:
Wow, this turned out amazing! The way you’ve captured the ethereal glow of the spectral blade with the embroidery really gives it that haunting yet elegant vibe. I love how the threads almost shimmer in the light, making it feel like the cutlass is ready to slice through the veil between worlds at any moment. It’s such a cool blend of old-school craftsmanship and fantasy lore.

I’m also impressed with how you handled the intricate details on the hilt and guard—those tiny flourishes really sell the mystic energy the weapon is supposed to have. It’s like your needle and thread have given life to something that was otherwise just a concept in the game’s background story. Have you thought about maybe adding a little glow-in-the-dark thread or something similar to make it pop even more in low light? I think that could take it to the next level.

Anyway, thanks for sharing this! It’s given me some serious inspiration for my own remaster project. If you ever decide to make one of those embroidered tarot cards from the Dreamcourt saga, count me in as the first to cheer on your page. Can’t wait to see what you create next!

The embroidery details along the hilt are so intricate, it gives the whole piece a sense of history and mystique. Definitely a step above any version I’ve seen modded into the game before.

I’m curious, did you have to rescale the textures yourself, or did the remaster tools do most of the heavy lifting? Either way, the end result speaks for itself. Can’t wait to see this in-game swinging through those spectral battles!

Wow, this turned out amazing! I love how you captured that ghostly shimmer on the blade — it really feels like the cutlass could slice through the fog in the Shadow Isles. Thanks for sharing this, it’s really inspiring to see such creative dedication in our community.
